question: Can owning a leading liquid major outright during its bullish USD cloud capture larger trends than BTC–ETH rotation?
single_variable: Expand the two-major cloud rotation to the nine alts plus BTC already named in the relative-pair study. At each 12H close for each USD-bullish asset count the fraction of other available peers against which its native close ratio has bullish EMA20/50, independently computing asset/peer for every direction. Each relative state needs 50 contiguous completed 12H bars, each built from 12 real BTC-clock native H1s for both legs. Compare highest fraction to lowest, or the alphabetically first eligible major. Preserve incumbents in tied sets to limit turnover; other ties alphabetical. Hold cash if no eligible candidate or the selected asset lacks its actual entry-hour open. Previously held exposure through an unobserved price gap fails validation.
account: Single shared wallet, 1000U, fully cash-funded 1x long only. Sell old then buy new at the following actual H1 open. Run 5bp per market fill and a second 5bp adverse-slip case. Use every H1 high and low witnessed by the one held coin, checking chronological lower and upper maximum drawdown. Chronological development, 2025, 2026 results. Hold cash before 50 bars and until a counterpart ratio is available.
selection_limit: Frozen named surviving group BTC, ETH, SOL, BNB, XRP, DOGE, ADA, LINK, LTC, AVAX, not a reconstructed point-in-time exchange-wide universe. Funding and executable order depth not modeled. This branch is an exploratory return path, not an executable whole-venue result.
